summary: Perf-canary false positive alerts after kernel-selection v2 metrics cardinality increase (label explosion)
description:
Issue summary:
Perf-canary rollout alerts for kernel auto-selection v2 started firing with no corresponding customer/user impact. Investigation shows alert query started evaluating on a much higher number of time series after kernel-selection v2 telemetry/metrics changes introduced additional high-cardinality labels.

Impact:
- False-positive pages to oncall (SRE + Runtime perf canary rotation) for ~3 hours.
- Canary gating looked “red” even though p95/p99 latency deltas were within expected bounds when aggregated correctly.
- Risk: masking real regressions due to alert fatigue / muted notifications.

What changed:
Kernel selection v2 instrumentation added labels including (examples): chosen_kernel, candidate_set_hash (or similar), kernel_registry_version, and sometimes raw model_id / model_revision in the metric dimension. The existing perf-canary alert rules grouped by several of these labels, which multiplied series count dramatically.

Observed symptoms:
- Alert: "perf-canary / kernel_selection_latency_regression" firing for multiple model/SKU combinations.
- Grafana panels for selection distribution showed 'No data' or extremely fragmented data due to series churn.
- Prometheus query cost increased (slow evaluations / partial results at peak).

Environment details:
- perf-canary runtime: 1.21.0-canary (kernel auto-selection v2 enabled behind gate)
- Regions observed: us-east primarily; also minor noise in eu-west dashboards (not paged)

Root cause:
Metric cardinality increased due to new kernel-selection labels being included as dimensions in time series. The alert and dashboard queries were written assuming stable, low-cardinality dimensions (model_family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket) and did not strip/aggregate over the new labels.

Fix plan:
1) Update alert queries (slo-toolkit / perf-canary rules) to aggregate over high-cardinality labels and only group by:
   - model_family (or canonical model_name)
   - gpu_sku (normalized)
   - seq_bucket (short/medium/long; prefill/decode regime)
   - (optional) region
   Explicitly drop/ignore: chosen_kernel, candidate_set_hash, model_revision, kernel_registry_version.

2) Update rollout dashboards to match the new recommended aggregation patterns and reduce panel query cost.

3) Add cardinality guardrails:
   - Recording rules for the common aggregates used in canary gating.
   - Add a lint/check in alert rule review: block queries that group by chosen_kernel or candidate_set_hash.

4) Follow-up: confirm runtime metrics adhere to "determinism and telemetry standards" (label allowlist + sampling policy) and document “safe labels for alerting”.

Acceptance criteria:
- Alerts stop firing under steady-state canary traffic (no manual muting required).
- Query evaluation time returns to baseline (<= 1s for key alert queries during normal load).
- Dashboards show stable, interpretable trends for p95/p99 deltas and selection distribution.

References:
- Slack: #eng-sre thread on rollout monitoring + sampling rate + rollback triggers (see 1769790024)
- Runtime telemetry PR: pr-28466
- Dashboard panels PR: observability-pack/pr-522
- Rollout SLO gates PR: slo-toolkit/pr-284
comments: 2026-02-14 09:12 Allison Grant (Reporter): Paging noise started after last night’s canary enablement. I’m seeing multiple kernel-selection v2 regression alerts firing, but the aggregate p99 on the main latency panel is flat. Suspecting metric cardinality change or label churn. Assigning to Caleb for PromQL / ingestion triage.

2026-02-14 09:28 Caleb Johnson: Confirmed high series count. The alert query currently groups by (model, gpu_sku, chosen_kernel, seq_bucket). chosen_kernel label now has ~8–15 values per (model,gpu) and candidate_set_hash appears in another metric used by the same rule. This is fragmenting the denominator and creating artificial deltas. Proposed fix: aggregate away chosen_kernel and any hash/version labels for alerting; keep those only in debug dashboards.

2026-02-14 09:44 Omar El-Sayed: +1. chosen_kernel is useful for debugging but should not be part of canary gating. For gating we only care about latency/err deltas per model_family/gpu/seq_bucket. Please also ensure we don’t include raw model_revision; that changes during canary experiments.

2026-02-14 10:05 Caleb Johnson: Drafted updated PromQL for the gating alerts. Example:
  - BEFORE: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model, gpu_sku, chosen_kernel, seq_bucket) (...))
  - AFTER:  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model_family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket, region) (...))
Also adding a recording rule for the aggregated histogram buckets so alert evaluation is cheap.

2026-02-14 11:22 Allison Grant: Please coordinate with Aisha (SLO dashboards) so the panels mirror the alert aggregation. We should avoid a situation where dashboard looks fine but alert groups on different labels.

2026-02-15 14:10 Caleb Johnson: Opened PR in slo-toolkit to update the alert rules and add recording rules. Also left review notes on observability-pack panels to avoid grouping by chosen_kernel unless on the dedicated debug dashboard. Requesting review from Allison + Aisha.

2026-02-16 09:03 Aisha Bello: Reviewed the rule change. Looks good. One request: keep gpu_sku normalization consistent with runtime (A100-80GB vs A100-80G) to avoid split series. Add label_replace mapping in the recording rule if needed.

2026-02-16 12:37 Caleb Johnson: Applied gpu_sku normalization in recording rule (canonical_gpu_sku). Deployed rules to perf-canary stack. Alert evaluation time dropped from ~8–12s to <1s. No new pages in the last 3 hours.

2026-02-17 08:20 Allison Grant: Confirmed: no further false positives overnight; dashboards are readable again. Marking resolved. Follow-up action item: add an "alert-safe labels" note to the kernel selection telemetry standards page and link it from the rollout dashboard doc.
resolution: Updated perf-canary alert queries and added recording rules to aggregate away high-cardinality kernel-selection v2 labels (chosen_kernel, candidate_set_hash, model_revision). Updated related dashboards to match alert aggregation. Alert noise stopped and query performance returned to baseline.
next_steps: Add 'alert-safe labels' guidance to kernel selection telemetry standards (include explicit denylist: chosen_kernel, candidate_set_hash, registry_version, model_revision). Owner: Allison Grant.
Add CI lint/check in slo-toolkit to flag grouping on known high-cardinality kernel-selection labels. Owner: Caleb Johnson.
Ensure runtime telemetry sampling policy is documented for chosen_kernel debug metrics to avoid unnecessary ingestion load. Owner: Logan Wright.
